raw_response:
Looking at my land and my life, I know what I'm doing this year. I've been farming this land for over forty years. My husband passed three years ago, my son works in Shijiazhuang. It's mostly just me now.

In Quzhou, everyone grows wheat and corn — that's the rotation here on the plain. Wheat goes in the ground in October, comes up through winter, we harvest in June. Then we put in corn right after on the same land, harvest in September. That's two crops a year off the same mu. That's what my mother did. That's what my neighbors do. I'm not going to try something different at my age.

I have about 7 mu. I'll put 6 mu into the wheat-corn rotation. The other half mu near the house I keep for garlic and some cabbage — that's for eating, not selling.

The wheat is already in the ground from last October. Now in spring I need to go out and water it once at jointing, maybe once more before heading if it's dry. I'll put down urea as a topdress — the bags from the village store. I'll spray for weeds in early spring and then spray fungicide before the wheat heads, because the last two years we had some rust problems.

For the corn, I'll wait until after wheat harvest, then I call the village machine station to rotary till. I buy hybrid seed — the dealer comes to the village and everyone buys from him. I don't know which variety exactly, whichever the dealer recommends is cheapest. I'll put in base fertilizer at planting, then topdress with urea at knee height. I water maybe twice if the summer rains don't come enough.

I'm 63, so I hire the tractor for ploughing and harvesting. My back can't do it. I do the spraying and the hand-weeding myself.
